features.name: Stance Fighter
features.text:
You can channel your inner resolve to shift into martial stances that grant you special benefits in combat.
Take the Martial Stances sheet and choose two martial stances from Tier 1. Each time you level up your character, choose an additional stance from your tier or lower.
You can spend a Focus to shift into a martial stance and gain its effects. You can shift only into stances you’ve marked as known. When you shift into a stance, it’s considered your active stance until you drop out of it.
You can’t shift into or have more than one active stance at a time. Until you shift into a stance, you are not considered to be in a stance or to have an active stance.
If you are already in a stance when you shift into a different stance, you automatically drop out of the previously active stance. You also drop out of your active stance when you take Severe damage or mark your last Hit Point. Otherwise, you drop out of your active stance at the end of the scene. When you drop out of a stance, you lose any ongoing benefits it provides.

features.text: When you’re traveling to a place you’ve previously visited or you carry an object that has been at the location before, you can identify the shortest, most direct path to your destination.

entries.name: Seraph: Winged Sentinel
entries.text: Play the Winged Sentinel if you want to take flight and strike crushing blows from the sky.

features.name: Ascendant
features.text: Gain a permanent +4 bonus to your Severe damage threshold.

features.name: Power of the Gods
features.text: While flying, you deal an extra **1d12** damage instead of 1d8 from your “Wings of Light” feature.

entries.name: Seraph: Winged Sentinel
entries.text: Play the Winged Sentinel if you want to take flight and strike crushing blows from the sky.

features.name: Ethereal Visage
features.text: Your supernatural visage strikes awe and fear. While flying, you have advantage on Presence Rolls. When you succeed with Hope on a Presence Roll, you can remove a Fear from the GM’s Fear pool instead of gaining Hope.

ui.label: Ethereal Visage
ui.description: Your supernatural visage strikes awe and fear. While flying, you have advantage on Presence Rolls. When you succeed with Hope on a Presence Roll, you can remove a Fear from the GM’s Fear pool instead of gaining Hope.

ui.label: Remove 1 GM Fear instead of Hope
ui.report: Removed {result.removed.amount} GM Fear instead of gaining Hope.

entries.name: Seraph: Winged Sentinel
entries.text: Play the Winged Sentinel if you want to take flight and strike crushing blows from the sky.

features.name: Wings of Light
features.text:
You can fly. While flying, you can do the following:

- **Mark a Stress** to pick up and carry another willing creature approximately your size or smaller.

- **Spend a Hope** to deal an extra **1d8** damage on a successful attack.

ui.label: Wings of Light
ui.description: Successful attack while flying.

entries.name: Bard: Wordsmith
entries.text: Play the Wordsmith if you want to use clever wordplay and captivate crowds.

features.name: Epic Poetry
features.text: Your Rally Die increases to a **d10**. Additionally, when you Help an Ally, you can narrate the moment as if you were writing the tale of their heroism in a memoir. When you do, roll a **d10** as your advantage die.

ui.label: Help an Ally: roll d10 advantage

entries.name: Bard: Wordsmith
entries.text: Play the Wordsmith if you want to use clever wordplay and captivate crowds.

features.name: Eloquent
features.text:
Your moving words boost morale. Once per session, when you encourage an ally, you can do one of the following:

- Allow them to find a mundane object or tool they need.

- Help an Ally without spending Hope.

- Give them an additional downtime move during their next rest.

entries.name: Bard: Wordsmith
entries.text: Play the Wordsmith if you want to use clever wordplay and captivate crowds.

features.name: Rousing Speech
features.text: Once per long rest, you can give a heartfelt, inspiring speech. All allies within Far range clear 2 Stress.

ui.label: Within Far range: clear 2 Stress
ui.report: {recipient.name} claimed Within Far range: clear 2 Stress.

features.name: Heart of a Poet
features.text: After you make an action roll to impress, persuade, or offend someone, you can **spend a Hope** to add a **d4** to the roll.

ui.label: Heart of a Poet
ui.description: Only to impress, persuade, or offend someone.

entries.name: Ranger
entries.text: As a ranger, your keen eyes and graceful haste make you indispensable when tracking down enemies and navigating the wilds.

features.name: Hold Them Off
features.text: **Spend 3 Hope** when you succeed on an attack with a weapon to use that same roll against two additional adversaries within range of the attack.

ui.label: Hold Them Off
ui.description: Use after a successful weapon attack: apply that same attack roll to two additional adversaries within its range.

features.name: Ranger’s Focus
features.text:
**Spend a Hope** and make an attack against a target. On a success, deal your attack’s normal damage and temporarily make the attack’s target your *Focus*. Until this feature ends or you make a different creature your *Focus*, you gain the following benefits against your *Focus*:

- You know precisely what direction they are in.

- When you deal damage to them, they must mark a Stress.

- When you fail an attack against them, you can end your Ranger’s Focus feature to reroll your Duality Dice.

ranger-s-focus.label: Ranger’s Focus
ranger-s-focus.text: Your attacks against your Focus can be rerolled once by ending this feature.

ranger-s-focus-2.label: Ranger’s Focus
ranger-s-focus-2.text: Your attacks against your Focus can be rerolled once by ending this feature.

ui.label: Ranger’s Focus
ui.description: Spend a Hope on this attack; on a success the target becomes your Focus.

ui.label: Ranger’s Focus: reroll (ends the feature)
ui.description: Reroll a failed attack against your Focus.

entries.name: Warrior
entries.text: As a warrior, you run into battle without hesitation or caution, knowing you can strike down whatever enemy stands in your path.

features.name: No Mercy
features.text: **Spend 3 Hope** to gain a +1 bonus to your attack rolls until your next rest.

ui.label: No Mercy
ui.description: +1 to attack rolls until your next rest.

features.name: Attack of Opportunity
features.text:
If an adversary within Melee range attempts to leave that range, make a reaction roll using a trait of your choice against their Difficulty. Choose one effect on a success, or two if you critically succeed:

- They can’t move from where they are.

- You deal damage to them equal to your primary weapon’s damage.

- You move with them.

features.name: Combat Training
features.text: You ignore burden when equipping weapons. When you deal physical damage, you gain a bonus to your damage roll equal to your level.

ui.label: Combat Training
ui.description: Physical damage only; weapon burden is ignored when equipping weapons.

entries.name: Seraph
entries.text: As a seraph, you’ve taken a vow to a god who helps you channel sacred arcane power to keep your party on their feet.

features.name: Life Support
features.text: **Spend 3 Hope** to clear a Hit Point on an ally within Close range.

features.name: Prayer Dice
features.text: At the beginning of each session, roll a number of **d4s** equal to your subclass’s Spellcast trait and place them on your character sheet in the space provided. These are your Prayer Dice. You can spend any number of Prayer Dice to aid yourself or an ally within Far range. You can use a spent die’s value to reduce incoming damage, add to a roll’s result after the roll is made, or gain Hope equal to the result. At the end of each session, clear all unspent Prayer Dice.

ui.label: Spend Prayer Dice for Hope (+{die.face})
ui.report: {actor.name} spent a Prayer Dice die for {result.gained} Hope.

ui.label: Prayer Dice die: +{die.face}
ui.report: {actor.name} added a Prayer Dice die; the roll is now {result.aided.total}.

entries.name: Sorcerer
entries.text: As a sorcerer, you were born with innate magical power, and you’ve learned how to wield that power to get what you want.

features.name: Volatile Magic
features.text: **Spend 3 Hope** to reroll any number of your damage dice on an attack that deals magic damage.

features.name: Arcane Sense
features.text: You can sense the presence of magical people and objects within Close range.

features.name: Minor Illusion
features.text: Make a **Spellcast Roll (10)**. On a success, you create a minor visual illusion no larger than yourself within Close range. This illusion is convincing to anyone at Close range or farther.

features.name: Channel Raw Power
features.text:
Once per long rest, you can place a domain card from your loadout into your vault and choose to either:

- Gain Hope equal to the level of the card.

- Enhance a spell that deals damage, gaining a bonus to your damage roll equal to twice the level of the card.

channel-raw-power.label: Channel Raw Power
channel-raw-power.text: Spend this bonus on one damaging spell.

inputs.label: Domain card to send to the vault

options.label: Gain Hope equal to the card's level
Add twice the card's level to a spell's damage

ui.label: Channel Raw Power
ui.description: Use on one spell that deals damage.

entries.name: Assassin
entries.text: As an assassin, you blend expertise in stealth and a mastery over death, dealing fatal blows tothe unwary with lethal accuracy.

features.name: Deadly Determination
features.text: **Spend 3 Hope** to clear 2 Stress.

features.name: Marked For Death
features.text:
On a successful weapon attack, you can **mark a Stress** to make the target *Marked for Death*. When you deal damage to a target you’ve *Marked for Death*, add a number of **d4s** equal to your tier to the damage roll.
You can have only one adversary *Marked for Death* at a time. This condition lasts until you take a rest, the current adversary *Marked for Death* is defeated, or the GM spends a number of Fear equal to your tier to clear it.

marked-for-death.label: Marked for Death
marked-for-death.text: One adversary is marked. Select the damage bonus only against that adversary. Remove this effect when the adversary is defeated or the GM spends Fear equal to your tier to clear the mark.

marked-for-death-2.label: Marked for Death
marked-for-death-2.text: One adversary is marked. Select the damage bonus only against that adversary. Remove this effect when the adversary is defeated or the GM spends Fear equal to your tier to clear the mark.

ui.label: Marked for Death
ui.description: Select only when damaging the adversary you have marked.

ui.label: Marked For Death
ui.description: Use after a successful weapon attack to mark that target.

features.name: Get In & Get Out
features.text: **Spend a Hope** to ask the GM for a quick or inconspicuous way into or out of a place you can see. The next roll you make that acts on this information has advantage.

entries.name: Witch
entries.text: As a witch, you use detailed knowledge of magical craft to weave spells that bolster your allies and hex your enemies.

features.name: Witch’s Charm
features.text: When you or an ally within Far range fails an action roll, you can **spend 3 Hope** to change it into a success with Fear instead.

features.name: Hex
features.text: **Mark a Stress** to temporarily *Hex* a target within Far range. While *Hexed*, the target gains a penalty to their damage rolls and Difficulty equal to your tier. The maximum number of creatures you can *Hex* at one time is equal to your Spellcast trait.

features.name: Commune
features.text:
Once per long rest during a moment of calm, you can commune with an ancestor, a deity, a spirit, or an otherworldly being. Ask them a question, then roll a number of **d6s** equal to your Spellcast trait. Choose one of the results and reference the chart below for the effect.

- **1-3:** You taste a flavor, smell a scent, or feel a sensation relevant to the answer.
- **4-5:** You hear sounds or see a vision relevant to the answer.
- **6:** You psychically experience a scene relevant to the answer as if you were there.

entries.name: Brawler
entries.text: As a brawler, you’ve honed your body into a lethal weapon, allowing you to deliverpowerful strikes that intimidate your foes.

features.name: Square Up
features.text: **Spend 3 Hope** to intimidate a target within Close range, making them temporarily *Vulnerable*.

features.name: I Am The Weapon
features.text: Your barehanded attacks are as strong as any blade. You have a primary weapon called Brawler’s Strike equipped while you have no other Active Weapons. It uses a trait of your choice, has Melee range, and deals **d8+d6** physical damage using your Proficiency (both the d8 and d6 scale off your Proficiency). While this weapon is active, you gain a +1 bonus to your Evasion.

features.name: Combo Strike
features.text:
After rolling damage on a successful attack with a Melee weapon, you can **mark a Stress** to start a combo strike. When you do, roll your Combo Die and note the result, then continue rolling your Combo Die until the result of your latest roll is lower than the roll that preceded it. You deal extra damage equal to the total of all rolled Combo Die results on this attack. The results can’t be modified by any means.
Your Combo Die starts as a **d4**. Once per tier, you can increase your Combo Die by one step as a level advancement option.

entries.name: Bard
entries.text: As a bard, you know how to get people to talk, bring attention to yourself, and use words or music to influence the world around you.

features.name: Make a Scene
features.text: **Spend 3 Hope** to temporarily *Distract* a target within Close range, giving them a -2 penalty to their Difficulty.

features.name: Rally
features.text:
Once per session, describe how you rally the party and give yourself and each of your allies a Rally Die. At level 1, your Rally Die is a **d6**. A PC can spend their Rally Die to roll it, adding the result to their action roll, reaction roll, damage roll, or to clear a number of Stress equal to the result. At the end of each session, clear all unspent Rally Dice.
At level 5, your Rally Die increases to a **d8**.

rally-die.label: Rally Die
rally-die.text: Spend this die on one action, reaction or damage roll, or to clear Stress.

entries.name: Blood Hunter
entries.text: As a blood hunter, you harness the power of hemocraft—that is, blood magic—in your relentless pursuit of evil creatures.

features.name: Blood Maledict
features.text: Spend 3 Hope to target a creature within Far range or in a vision from your Grim Psychometry. Until you finish a rest, take Severe damage, or use this feature again, you have advantage on all action rolls against the target.

blood-maledict.label: Blood Maledict
blood-maledict.text: Advantage on action rolls against your chosen target. Ends on Severe damage, a rest, or reuse.

ui.label: Blood Maledict advantage
ui.description: Only against the chosen target.

features.name: Crimson Rite
features.text: You can enchant your strikes with bloodthirsty power at the cost of your vitality. Mark a Hit Point to enchant one of your active weapons. Until you finish your next rest, that weapon deals physical or magic damage (choose when you use this feature) and an extra 1d6 damage when you hit with it. This extra damage increases to 2d6 at level 5 and 3d6 at level 8.

crimson-rite.label: Crimson Rite
crimson-rite.text: Optional extra damage for your enchanted strikes; weapon and damage type are table-managed.

features.name: Grim Psychometry
features.text: While inspecting a creature, a location, or an object within Very Close range, make a Spellcast Roll (12) . On a success, mark a Stress to have a vision of the most recent violence involving the target, and until you finish a rest, you have advantage on any action roll to recall lore about things in the vision.

grim-psychometry.label: Grim Psychometry
grim-psychometry.text: Advantage when recalling lore about things in the vision.

ui.label: Grim Psychometry: mark Stress for a vision
Vision lore advantage
ui.description: Only to recall lore about things in the vision.

entries.name: Druid
entries.text: As a druid, you are a force of nature, preserving the balance of life and death by channeling the wilds themselves through you.

features.name: Evolution
features.text: **Spend 3 Hope** to transform into a Beastform without marking a Stress. When you do, choose one trait to raise by +1 until you drop out of that Beastform.

features.name: Beastform
features.text: **Mark a Stress** to magically transform into a creature of your tier or lower from the Beastform list. You can drop out of this form at any time. While transformed, you can’t use weapons or cast spells from domain cards, but you can still use other features or abilities you have access to. Spells you cast before you transform stay active and last for their normal duration, and you can talk and communicate as normal. Additionally, you gain the Beastform’s features, add their Evasion bonus to your Evasion, and use the trait specified in their statistics for your attack. While you’re in a Beastform, your armor becomes part of your body and you mark Armor Slots as usual; when you drop out of a Beastform, those marked Armor Slots remain marked. If you mark your last Hit Point, you automatically drop out of this form.

features.name: Wildtouch
features.text: You can perform harmless, subtle effects that involve nature—such as causing a flower to rapidly grow, summoning a slight gust of wind, or starting a campfire—at will.

entries.name: Rogue
entries.text: As a rogue, you have experience fighting with your blade as well as your wit, preferring to move quickly and fight quietly.

features.name: Rogue’s Dodge
features.text: **Spend 3 Hope** to gain a +2 bonus to your Evasion until the next time an attack succeeds against you. Otherwise, this bonus lasts until your next rest.

features.name: Cloaked
features.text: Any time you would be *Hidden*, you are instead *Cloaked*. In addition to the benefits of the *Hidden* condition, while *Cloaked* you remain unseen if you are stationary when an adversary moves to where they would normally see you. After you make an attack or end a move within line of sight of an adversary, you are no longer *Cloaked*.

features.name: Sneak Attack
features.text: When you succeed on an attack while *Cloaked* or while an ally is within Melee range of your target, add a number of **d6s** equal to your tier to your damage roll.

ui.label: Sneak Attack
ui.description: Successful attack while Cloaked or an ally is in Melee of target.

entries.name: Guardian
entries.text: As a guardian, you run into danger to protect your party, keeping watch over those who might not survive without you there.

features.name: Frontline Tank
features.text: **Spend 3 Hope** to clear 2 Armor Slots.

features.name: Unstoppable
features.text:
Once per long rest, you can become *Unstoppable*. You gain an Unstoppable Die. At level 1, your Unstoppable Die is a **d4**. Place it on your character sheet in the space provided, starting with the 1 value facing up. After you make a damage roll that deals 1 or more Hit Points to a target, increase the Unstoppable Die value by one. When the die’s value would exceed its maximum value or when the scene ends, remove the die and drop out of *Unstoppable*. At level 5, your Unstoppable Die increases to a **d6**.
While *Unstoppable*, you gain the following benefits:

- You reduce the severity of physical damage by one threshold (Severe to Major, Major to Minor, Minor to None).

- You add the current value of the Unstoppable Die to your damage roll.

- You can’t be *Restrained* or *Vulnerable*.

unstoppable.label: Unstoppable
unstoppable.text: Add the current Unstoppable Die value to damage and reduce physical damage severity by one threshold. You cannot be Restrained or Vulnerable. Advance the die after a damage roll deals at least 1 HP; the buff ends on overflow or at scene end.

ui.label: Unstoppable: dealt HP - increase die
ui.description: Use only after this damage roll dealt at least 1 HP to a target.

ui.label: Unstoppable
ui.description: Reduces physical damage severity by one threshold: Severe to Major, Major to Minor, Minor to None. Magic damage is unaffected.

entries.name: Warlock
entries.text: As a warlock, you’ve pledged your life to an otherworldly patron in exchange for extraordinary power.

features.name: Patron’s Boon
features.text: When you fail a roll, you can **spend 3 Hope** to reroll with advantage.

features.name: Patron’s Pact
features.text: You have committed yourself to a supernatural entity—such as a god, fae, or demon—in exchange for power. Write their name on your character sheet, then work with your GM to determine their sphere of influence (such as Nature, Chaos, Wisdom, Mischief, Love, War, Justice, or Death). Before making an action roll that relates to your patron’s sphere of influence, you can **spend a Favor **to call upon their aid, rolling your Patron Die and adding its result to the total. Your Patron Die starts at a **d6** and increases to a **d8** at level 5.

ui.label: Patron Die
ui.description: Only an action related to your patron’s sphere of influence.

features.name: Favor
features.text: You start with 3 Favor. You can use a downtime move to show tribute to your patron. Describe how and gain Favor equal to your Spellcast trait. Additionally, when you succeed on an action roll with Hope, you can choose to gain a Favor instead of a Hope.

ui.label: Gain 1 Favor instead of Hope
ui.report: Gained 1 Favor instead of gaining Hope.

entries.name: Wizard
entries.text: As a wizard, you’ve become familiar with the arcane through the relentless study of grimoires and other tools of magic.

features.name: Not This Time
features.text: **Spend 3 Hope** to force an adversary within Far range to reroll an attack or damage roll.

features.name: Prestidigitation
features.text: You can perform harmless, subtle magical effects at will. For example, you can change an object’s color, create a smell, light a candle, cause a tiny object to float, illuminate a room, or repair a small object.

features.name: Strange Patterns
features.text: Choose a number between 1 and 12. When you roll that number on a Duality Die, gain a Hope or clear a Stress. You can change this number when you take a long rest.

ui.label: Strange Patterns: gain a Hope
ui.description: A Duality Die matches your chosen number.

ui.label: Strange Patterns: clear a Stress
ui.description: A Duality Die matches your chosen number.
